skill.name: security-scanning-tools
skill.description: Guides authorized security teams through vulnerability scanning, network discovery, web application testing, wireless assessment, malware scanning, cloud checks, and compliance validation.
skill.summary: Plan and document authorized security scanning workflows across common assessment tools.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The Markdown backtick and some reference-table matches are false positives, but the skill contains extensive confirmed active scanning guidance. High-risk content includes Nmap and Masscan workflows, sudo-based tooling, command-line API key exposure, Metasploit exploitation validation, Internet-wide scanning, and wireless deauthentication or password cracking.

remediation.suggestion: Remove exploit execution and auto-exploitation guidance, or replace it with non-exploit validation steps and strict authorization requirements.

remediation.issue: Wireless deauthentication and password cracking commands
remediation.suggestion: Remove attack and cracking commands, or limit the section to defensive detection concepts and lab-only references.
Replace 0.0.0.0/0 and high-rate Masscan examples with reserved documentation ranges and explicit rate, scope, and permission checks.
Add human confirmation requirements before sudo commands and separate install, service, wireless, and audit steps from agent-executable workflows.

remediation.issue: API key and sensitive report handling
remediation.suggestion: Avoid command-line API keys and shared temporary report paths; use protected configuration files and private output directories instead.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Internet-Wide High-Rate Scanning Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The Masscan section includes a large-scale scan against 0.0.0.0/0 with a rate of 100000. This teaches Internet-wide probing unless the user replaces it with a tightly authorized scope.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The line directly targets the entire IPv4 space and sets a high packet rate, so the operational risk is explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Wireless Deauthentication and Password Cracking Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The Aircrack-ng section gives steps for deauthentication attacks and WPA or WEP cracking. These instructions can disrupt networks and support unauthorized credential attacks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The section labels deauthentication as an attack and then provides concrete cracking commands, leaving little ambiguity about offensive capability.

semantic_findings.title: Exploit Validation and Auto-Exploitation Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The Metasploit section says to validate vulnerabilities with exploitation and includes commands to select an SMB scanner, run it, and suggest exploits. This goes beyond passive vulnerability assessment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly references exploitation and Metasploit workflow steps, including exploit suggestion through analyze.

content.value_statement: Security teams need consistent methods for authorized vulnerability scans and assessment reports. This skill organizes common tools, workflows, outputs, and reporting steps for controlled security reviews.
actual_capabilities: Outlines phased workflows for network discovery, vulnerability scanning, web testing, and compliance checks.
Lists common commands for tools such as Nmap, Masscan, Nessus, OpenVAS, ZAP, Nikto, Lynis, and OpenSCAP.
Explains expected report types, including network discovery, vulnerability, web application, and compliance reports.
Provides tool selection guidance by assessment scenario and scanning category.
Summarizes legal considerations, technical limits, troubleshooting steps, and reporting structure.
limitations: The skill does not verify authorization, scope, or ownership of targets.
Some examples describe active, intrusive, or offensive scanning techniques.
Commands require installed third-party tools and suitable operating system permissions.
Findings from automated tools still require expert validation before action.

use_cases.title: Plan an Internal Scan
use_cases.description: Define scope, choose discovery tools, and outline expected outputs for an approved internal network review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Web Assessment
use_cases.description: Select web scanners, proxy workflows, and reporting steps for an authorized application security test.

use_cases.title: Document Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Map compliance scanners and report formats to evidence needed for audit preparation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Scanning Tools
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an authorized assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: I have written authorization to assess this environment. Help me choose scanning tools for scope: [scope], asset types: [assets], and required report format: [format].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Scan Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a phased scanning plan for an authorized security review. Include discovery, vulnerability checks, validation steps, reporting outputs, and safety limits.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Tool Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Nmap, Nessus, OpenVAS, ZAP, Nikto, Lynis, and OpenSCAP for this authorized assessment: [goals]. Explain overlap, gaps, and reporting value.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Controlled Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a controlled scanning methodology for authorized network, web, cloud, and compliance testing. Include scope controls, risk limits, validation, and executive reporting.

output_examples.input: Plan an authorized internal network vulnerability assessment for a small office subnet.
output: Scope summary with authorized assets and excluded systems.
Discovery, service identification, vulnerability scanning, validation, and reporting phases.
A report outline covering key findings, affected services, risk ratings, and remediation priorities.

output_examples.input: Choose tools for a web application security review with authenticated areas.
output: Recommended use of proxy-based testing, crawling, passive review, active checks, and manual validation.
Notes about authentication setup, scope boundaries, rate limits, and evidence collection.
A concise report structure for OWASP-style findings and remediation guidance.

output_examples.input: Prepare compliance scanning evidence for Linux servers.
output: Suggested compliance scanner categories and profile selection steps.
Evidence requirements for scan reports, exceptions, and remediation tracking.
Operational cautions about privileged access and production system impact.

best_practices: Use written authorization and explicit scope before any scan.
Start with passive or low-impact checks before intrusive tests.
Validate automated findings manually before reporting or remediation.
anti_patterns: Do not scan public or third-party systems without permission.
Do not run high-rate scans against production networks without change approval.
Do not treat exploit validation as routine vulnerability confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill run scans by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples. Users remain responsible for tools, permissions, and target authorization.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for public targets?
faq.answer: No. It should only be used for systems where the user has explicit written authorization.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers tools including Nmap, Masscan, Nessus, OpenVAS, Burp Suite, ZAP, Nikto, Aircrack-ng, ClamAV, Prowler, ScoutSuite, Lynis, and OpenSCAP.

faq.question: Can it help create reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes report types, output formats, and a basic executive summary structure.

faq.question: Does it confirm vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It explains validation concepts, but expert review is required before declaring a confirmed vulnerability.

faq.question: Why are some examples restricted?
faq.answer: Some examples involve intrusive scanning, privileged commands, wireless disruption, or exploitation workflows that can harm systems without permission.
